Record date: 2129-09-05
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 09/05/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath, persistent cough with increased sputum production, and significant bilateral lower extremity swelling.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for reevaluation following yesterday's assessment for his COPD exacerbation and CHF management. The patient reports a marked deterioration in his respiratory status, experiencing increased shortness of breath even at rest, necessitating continuous supplemental oxygen. He describes his cough as more productive today, with a notable increase in the volume of yellow-green sputum, and he continues to experience intermittent fevers, which have recurred more frequently since the last visit.
Mr. Fairfax expresses heightened fatigue, which he attributes to the increased respiratory effort and poor sleep quality. He reports nocturnal awakenings have increased again, and he feels that the bilateral lower extremity edema has worsened, with significant discomfort and difficulty ambulating.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, + weight gain (approx. 3 lbs since last visit), + fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + worsening shortness of breath at rest, + increased productive cough with yellow-green sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, + orthopnea, + paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 150/88 mmHg - Heart Rate: 98 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 30 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 84% on supplemental oxygen.
General: The patient appears significantly fatigued and in moderate respiratory distress, using accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, with pronounced wheezing and bilateral crackles throughout; increased respiratory effort noted.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: Severe bilateral lower extremity edema with significant pitting, extending to the groin, with tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation, worsening with increased sputum production; pneumonia remains a strong possibility pending further investigation. 2. Congestive heart failure with significant fluid overload; current diuretic therapy is inadequate for symptom relief. 3. Insomnia exacerbated by respiratory distress and discomfort; pharmacological intervention is warranted.
PLAN
1. Order a chest X-ray to evaluate for pneumonia and assess for potential effusions; consider CT chest if findings are inconclusive. 2. Initiate intravenous furosemide at 100 mg for rapid diuresis; adjust dosing based on response and renal function. 3. Continue azithromycin for a total of 5 days; if pneumonia is confirmed, reassess antibiotic therapy. 4. Start systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 40 mg daily) to manage COPD exacerbation and reduce airway inflammation. 5. Increase nebulized treatments to every 4 hours with albuterol and budesonide, and continue ipratropium bromide. 6. Discuss potential admission to the hospital for closer monitoring and treatment of his respiratory status and CHF; this will be contingent on response to the immediate interventions. 7. Initiate trazodone 50 mg at bedtime for sleep disturbances, monitoring for efficacy and side effects. 8. Reinforce education on recognizing signs of respiratory distress, importance of adherence to medications, and the need for immediate medical attention should symptoms escalate.
Mr. Fairfax demonstrated understanding of the treatment modifications and the rationale for hospitalization.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was advised to be admitted to the hospital for further management and monitoring of his respiratory and cardiac conditions. A bed was requested, and the patient was prepared for transport. A follow-up appointment will be determined based on his hospital course and recovery.
